channel.title: WSJ | World
channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: World Court Finds Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
item.description: The landmark judgment is the first time a state has been found legally responsible for seeking to destroy an ethnic or religious minority.

item.title: The Morning Risk Report: The Jensen Huang Saga Has Reinvigorated Washington’s China Hawks
item.description: Plus: Microsoft-Bytedance cloud deal under fire from lawmakers and EU anti-money-laundering, public prosecution bodies team up.

item.title: Insurgents in Iran’s Borderlands Are Becoming a Bigger Challenge for the Regime
item.description: A series of attacks by ethnic insurgent groups is squeezing Iran’s leaders, who are already under pressure from the war and U.S. blockade.

item.title: Trump Says ‘We Are Really Making History’ at First-Ever Summit With Xi, Putin
item.description: The three leaders sat down in Shenzhen, China, for a show of unity that highlights shifts in global leadership.

item.title: Wall Street Pledged $500 Billion for Nvidia. Not a Dollar Has Been Deployed.
item.description: Plus,Trump, Xi and Putin met in their first-ever summit, and Anthropic sells more shares than it planned at a higher price than expected for its IPO.

item.title: Houthi Attack Damages Saudi Capital’s Tallest Tower
item.description: The strike damaged several floors in the 80-story building which houses the kingdom’s sovereign-wealth fund.

item.title: UniCredit Strikes Deal With Germany to Clear Path for Commerzbank Takeover
item.description: The Italian bank agreed to keep Commerzbank headquarters in Frankfurt—where the bank will remain listed on the stock exchange—and Germany will no longer seek to directly nominate members to Commerzbank’s board.

item.title: Asian Equities Mixed Amid Cautious Market Sentiment
item.description: Expectations for higher interest rates and renewed concerns over technology stocks kept investors cautious.

item.title: The Jensen Huang Saga Has Reinvigorated Washington’s China Hawks
item.description: The AI spy affair has spurred once-sidelined politicians to get tough on China.

item.title: European Defense Chief Snaps at Pentagon Official Over Ukraine Criticism
item.description: A NATO meeting aimed at boosting unity in support of Ukraine turned snippy when a top European defense chief called a U.S. official’s criticism of Kyiv’s strikes “stupid.”

item.title: Hegseth Cements New Military Deal in Visit to Venezuela
item.description: The defense secretary signed the agreement with Caracas’s interim government, during a trip that wasn’t announced beforehand by the Pentagon.

item.title: Europe Ditched Russian Fuel. Now It’s Hooked on Chinese Green Tech Instead.
item.description: Big price gaps on electric cars and solar gear have left the continent struggling to protect local factories.

item.title: See How Ukraine Hit Putin’s Showpiece Bridge
item.description: A sophisticated attack using mostly Ukrainian-made drones and missiles badly damaged Russia’s bridge to occupied Crimea.

item.title: U.S. Enters Unprecedented Three-Way Nuclear Rivalry With China and Russia
item.description: Beijing’s rapid weapons buildup is forcing Washington to prepare to face two major nuclear powers for the first time.

item.title: BOE’s Bailey Sees Length of Iran War as Key to Rate Path
item.description: The BOE earlier this month raised its key interest rate for the first time since the war began, becoming the last of its peers to tighten policy in response to higher energy prices.

item.title: Iran Attacks Kuwait and Bahrain, Further Escalating Fight Over Strait
item.description: Tehran’s attacks come after it set a natural gas tanker ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz and as a quiet campaign of U.S. strikes continues.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of November 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
item.description: President Trump began his visit to a city that is China’s answer to Silicon Valley, home to drones, robotaxis and some of the country’s biggest tech giants.

item.title: Nvidia’s Strong Results Do Little to Settle Questions About Its Future
item.description: Plus, parents spend a fortune to turn 6-year-olds into F1 drivers, and a cascade of outages triggers conspiracy theories—and finger pointing.

item.title: U.S. Energy Chief Urges Western Europe to Pivot to Power Expansion
item.description: Western Europe has done too little to grow its energy resources—and needs an energy-addition mindset—according to U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright.
